title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills are being mailed out on Monday.  The due date for mobile home taxes will be July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you do not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].  That will give the office time to investigate the matter before it is at risk of becoming delinquent.

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Xenia Village Board met in regular session last night with the board of trustees appointing Trustee Galen Garrison to lead the meeting. The appointment came about due to acting Mayor Dewight Casolari submitting his letter of resignation from the position on April 9th.  While no reason for Mr. Casolaris resignation was given trustees voted to accept Mr. Casolari’s resignation.

Trustees quickly approved the treasures reports, April bills and payroll before taking public comments.  In public comments Brandon Bridges with Charleston engineering, and son of late village engineer Mike Bridges, informed trustees what it would cost the city to soil cement certain village roads which present an issue for residents.  These areas are separate projects from the ones the village received funding for through IDOT.  Mr. Bridges Informed Trustees that to soil cement from 5 Street to Church and Cottonwood the estimated cost would be $47,000.  While the cost of soil cement on 200 feet on Main Street would cost the village.  When asked by trustees if MFT might cover the cost of the work Bridges remarked “it may cover some.”

Trustees then turned their attention to village properties approving a letter to be sent out to several residents whose properties are in violation of one or multiple village ordinances.  Trustees are hopeful that sending out ordnance violation notices ahead of city wide clean up in May residents will more easily be able to bring their properties up to code.  Trustees also discussed raising the rates on the Villages water sewer and trash sending out a letter to residents detailing the changes.

In police business officer Jerry Burkett told trustees the police cruiser needed regular maintenance and brakes.  Xenia village employees also received Long awaited news on the IMRF and expect to be approved by June.

Xenia and Residents from Ironwood to Charley Brown Park will be under a boil order beginning 9 am Tuesday April 21st.  The boil order is the result of needed repairs and replacement of a fire hydrant in Charley Brown Park.

Last on the village board of trustees’ agenda was the discussion to appoint a new mayor.  It was decided that Galen Garrison would take the position of acting mayor until the time of the next village election when another suitable candidate can be found.

title: CREDIT CARD SCAM
full_story:
First Community Bank of Xenia Flora is warning customers of an ongoing scam.

The bank has been informed that a person has received a phone call which appeared to be from First Community Bank about a credit card application.  The caller ID made it appear that the call was coming from the Flora Branch.  First Community Bank is advising people who receive such calls to hang up, and call the bank directly.  They will never ask you to provide personal information over the phone.

Anyone who has been a victim of a scam is encouraged to contact their financial institution and report the incident to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center at www.ic3.gov or the Federal Trade Commission at www.ftc.gov.

title: CEO TRADE SHOW
full_story:
The Clay County CEO (Creating Entrepreneurial Opportunities) Class of 2026 will host its annual Trade Show on Wednesday, April 29, from 5:00 to 7:00 PM at the New Beginnings Church in Flora, where nine student entrepreneurs will showcase the individual businesses, they have developed throughout the school year.

The trade show represents the culmination of a year-long experience in which students learn the fundamentals of business by creating and operating their own ventures.  Community members are invited to attend, meet the students, and explore a wide variety of products and services created by local high school seniors.

Andrew Shelby, owner of HydroHoops, offers custom hydrodipped basketballs that feature unique, eye-catching designs, helping players easily identify their ball while expressing personal style.

Carder Walden created G2G (Glory to God), a Christian bracelet brand featuring high-quality woven bracelets with Bible verses printed on the inside, designed to inspire faith and spark meaningful conversations.

Chloe Whitmire, owner of Chloe’s Cleaning Co., provides residential and commercial cleaning services focused on reliability, attention to detail, and creating clean, welcoming environments.

Ella Cammon operates Essentials by Ella, a business that designs and sells organized, easy-to-use emergency car kits aimed at helping drivers feel safe and prepared for unexpected situations.

Halle Kitley brings creativity to the forefront with Patched Hat Bar, where customers can design their own custom trucker hats using a variety of patches and styles.

Haven Cash founded The Growing Point, a gardening brand offering curated boxes with seeds, guidance, and resources to help individuals and families learn and succeed in gardening.

Mason Byers, owner of Better Bites, produces protein balls and healthy snacks made with quality ingredients, offering a convenient and nutritious option for busy lifestyles.

Noah Hatcher created Fore You Golf, a custom golf accessory brand that allows golfers to personalize items such as balls, tees, markers, and towels.

Parker Helm launched LATHR, a men’s grooming brand specializing in high-quality scented soap bars designed to deliver premium fragrances and a refined grooming experience.

The Clay County CEO program emphasizes real-world learning by connecting students with local business leaders, providing mentorship opportunities, and allowing students to experience entrepreneurship firsthand.  The Trade Show serves as a final opportunity for students to present their work, engage with customers, and put their skills into action.

Community members are encouraged to attend and support these young entrepreneurs as they take an important step toward their futures in business and beyond.

The CEO Class will be the guests today on the ReVue talking about their businesses.

title: YOUTH TURKEY HUNTERS SET RECORD
full_story:
Illinois youth turkey hunters set a new record, harvesting a preliminary total of 2,318 birds during the 2025 Illinois youth season.  The total surpasses last year’s record of 2,099 birds and marks the third consecutive year of record-setting youth turkey harvest in Illinois.

Clay County turkey hunters killed 62 birds, 12 more than last year and the 5th most in the state.  Fayette county hunters were 2nd in the state with 74, 11 more than last year.  Marion County were 3rd in the state with 68, twenty more than last year.  Wayne County hunters took 52 birds, 4 more than last year.  Effingham County youth took 42 birds the same as last year, Jasper County hunter took 30 birds 2 more than last year and Richland County hunters only shot 8 birds, 9 less than last year.

Participation also reached an all-time high this spring.  Youth hunters purchased a record 7,369 permits in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 6,538 sold in 2025.  Along with a success rate of over 30% for the third year in a row, the increasing totals reflect strong youth interest in turkey hunting, excellent hunting opportunities and a robust statewide turkey population.

This year’s youth season was March 28th and 29th and April 4th and 5th.  The top five counties for youth harvest were Jefferson, 75; Fayette, 74; Marion, 68; Adams, 62; and Clay, 62.

title: NORTH WAYNE PRESCHOOL SCREENING
full_story:
The North Wayne Schools are conducting Child Find/Preschool screening for three to five-year-old children not yet enrolled in public schools and who will not be Kindergarten eligible in the fall.

The screening checks each child’s progress in hearing, vision, speech, language, and coordination skills.  This will give parents a better idea of how their child is progressing at this very young age before he/she begins school.  This screening program is free, and parents will receive immediate feedback on how their child is developing.  Head Start personnel may also be present to explain their program and services.

The Child Find/Preschool Screening will be held at Johnsonville on April 20th, from 8:30 am to 2:30 pm.  The screening procedure takes about 45 minutes, and appointments must be made so that children do not have a long wait period.  Parents should call 618-673-3044 to make an appointment or to get more information.

The service is a free check of your child’s progress in the development areas, but appointments are needed.  If you live in the North Wayne School District call 618-673-3044 to make an appointment for your preschooler.

title: IECC SUMMER CAMPS
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges (IECC) is excited to announce the release of its 2026 Summer Camps and 2026–2027 Community Education Catalog, offering engaging learning opportunities for students of all ages across the district.

This summer, IECC will offer a wide variety of hands-on camps designed for elementary through high school students.  Led by IECC faculty and community experts, the camps focus on creativity, exploration, and career discovery in a fun and supportive environment.

Camp highlights include, STEM and technology camps such as LEGO Battle Bots, 3D Printing, and Broadband: From Cell Towers to Smartphones.  Creative arts experiences including Origami, Drawing, Watercolor, and Canvas Painting.  Career exploration camps like Forensic Science, Culinary Conquest, Cosmetology, and Media Production, and Unique learning opportunities such as Sign Language, Mandarin Chinese, and Theater Tech.

These camps help students build confidence, strengthen problem-solving skills, and gain early awareness of possible career paths while enjoying hands-on learning experiences.

Beyond summer programs, IECC’s Community Education offerings continue year-round, supporting lifelong learning and strengthening local communities through accessible and meaningful classes.

Community Education programs include, Personal enrichment classes such as art, sewing, woodworking, and fitness, Workforce and career development programs, including the SkillForge Manufacturing Skills Lab, Music ensembles, book clubs, and community groups, and Online courses in areas like computer skills, languages, and game development.

Whether individuals want to learn a new skill, explore a hobby, advance their careers, or connect with others, IECC’s Community Education programs offer something for everyone.

Registration is available through Student Services at each IECC campus.

Full details, including course descriptions and schedules, can be found in the Community Education Catalog at www.iecc.edu/communityed.

title: GAS TAX HOLIDAY PROPOSED
full_story:
Illinois Republican representatives spoke out in Springfield Wednesday during a press conference on Illinois’ gas tax as prices climb to over $4 per gallon.

Representative Ryan Spain and Representative Regan Deering proposed House Bill 5738, a measure they called relief for working families, citing ongoing affordability concerns.  Their proposal would create a six-month “holiday” on the sales tax applied to gasoline, from July 1st through December 31st.

Illinois’ gas tax automatically increases each July.  As of July 2025, it reached 48.3 cents per gallon, the second highest in the country, with another increase expected this July.

Spain said if approved, the measure could lower gas prices by about 20 cents per gallon by pausing the sales tax, but not the motor fuel tax.  The state’s gas tax is five cents per dollar, per gallon.

He added that State Republicans had suggested the 5% sales tax funds be moved from the general revenue fund to the road fund to provide investments in Illinois roads.

However, the proposal was dropped in the Transit Reform Package conducted during veto session in Springfield, meaning funds from customers at the pump will now be directed to mass transit, primarily in Chicago.

Spain said “Downstate has seen systemic disinvestment in our road and bridge infrastructure over the past several decades, but this escalated when Democrats seized sales taxes on motor fuel and interest from unspent road funds to support Chicago-area mass transit systems.”

The bill is currently sitting in the Rules Committee and, if passed, would take effect immediately.
